issue_context.title: labelkeep dropping internal labels
issue_context.body:
### What did you do?

Use labelkeep to set a list of allowed labels

### What did you expect to see?

only allowed labels in regex would appear

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

nothing, as the target got into problems because labelkeep was dropping required labels

For example:


to avoid these issues

comments: Mmh I wonder when we introduced this regreassion. Maybe we should fallback if those labels are unset somehow. cc @LeviHarrison WDYT?

Thanks for the report.

Looking into the code, this appears to work as expected. For other relabeling operations, users do expect internal labels to be taken into consideration as well. The doc also mentions that relabeling applies to all labels, as stated here https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/configuration/#relabel_config (It might be beneficial to make this more explicit? add some warnings?)

This behavior has been consistent since the beginning, https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/commit/d7f4f8b879c6fde3f069450ee11a4bbe63e32761#diff-cfa58e94d6a84339db19dcd506b883c05fee7211038ca07246d608707c49f4e9R328 IIUC. (but maybe it was readjusted and then reverted in between)

Note that this "issue" doesn't go unnoticed. The `prometheus_target_sync_failed_total` metric is incremented (monitored by `PrometheusTargetSyncFailure`) when the address label is dropped or invalid, or when other internal labels are dropped or invalid.

I've added a test in this https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/15529 to reinforce the behavior/doc.

I believe any changes to this should be considered as a feature.
isn't this a huge footgun? one would need to always add the required labels to use labelkeep or you will just not get anything

If you don't get anything, it's a very obvious failure, and it is easy to fix. That's not what we usually call a footgun.

A footgun is more something that looks useful in a certain situation but explodes in your face in the worst possible moment later.

I would just call the current behavior a bit clunky, but it's nevertheless consistent. We could start a debate if we want to add another flavor of `labelkeep` or add a feature flag to change its behavior, but we cannot really change the current behavior without a major version bump.
